quote: Under AHEAD, CMMI would have set global budget baselines for hospitals from their historical Medicare FFS spending, with adjustments; Act 68's global budgets inherit the same benchmark logic.
correct_fact: AHEAD provided prospective Medicare FFS hospital global budgets with quality adjustments; Act 68 directs GMCB to set global hospital budget standards that 'reflect the implementation of reference-based pricing and the total cost of care targets' -- it does not adopt AHEAD's Medicare-FFS historical baseline, and GMCB has not published a global budget revenue-setting rule.
source_quote: Act 68 Sec. 2 (18 V.S.A. 9375(b)(7)): 'including establishing standards for global hospital budgets that reflect the implementation of reference-based pricing and the total cost of care targets determined in collaboration with federal partners and other stakeholders or as set by the Statewide Health Care Delivery Plan'. CMS AHEAD: 'annual, prospective Medicare fee-for-service global budgets, covering inpatient and outpatient services.'
proposed_new_text: Under AHEAD, CMMI would have set prospective Medicare FFS global budgets for hospitals. Act 68 instead directs GMCB to set global budget standards that reflect reference-based pricing and the state's total cost of care targets; the revenue-setting methodology has not yet been published.
notes: 'Inherit the same benchmark logic' has no basis in Act 68. The second sentence of the callout (lower-spending hospitals face limited upside) is a reasonable general inference, left.

quote: GMCB's reference-based pricing uses Medicare rates as the external benchmark --- not Vermont hospital historical prices.
correct_fact: Act 68 requires RBP prices to be based on a percentage of Medicare or another benchmark.
source_quote: Reference-based prices established pursuant to this subsection (e) shall be based on a percentage of the Medicare reimbursement for the same or a similar item or service or on another benchmark, as appropriate
notes: Statute also allows 'another benchmark' and requires GMCB to consider acuity, payer mix, labor costs etc. per hospital. RBP does not apply to Medicare or Medicaid patients (Sec. 3, 9376(e)(6)).

quote: Vermont's Act 68 global budgets for non-CAH hospitals must specify how the prospective budget is set and adjusted for patient complexity --- the risk adjustment methodology is a key design question currently under development.
correct_fact: Act 68's global budget provision contains no requirement to specify a patient-complexity/risk adjustment. It requires global budgets for one or more non-CAH hospitals by HFY2028 'to the extent that resources are available', all hospitals by HFY2030, including Medicare where federal law permits but not Medicaid. The acuity/payer-mix/social-risk factors in Act 68 attach to reference-based pricing, not global budgets.
source_quote: (B)(i) Beginning not later than hospital fiscal year 2028, to the extent that resources are available, the Board shall establish global hospital budgets for one or more Vermont hospitals that are not critical access hospitals. ... (ii) Global hospital budgets established pursuant to this section shall include Medicare to the extent permitted under federal law but shall not include Medicaid.
proposed_new_text: Act 68 does not prescribe how a global budget is set or adjusted for patient complexity --- GMCB has not yet published that methodology, so risk adjustment remains a key open design question for the first non-CAH global budgets.
notes: Act 68 does require GMCB to weigh acuity, payer mix and social risk when setting each hospital's reference-based prices (9376(e)(2)(B)).

quote: Includes all Medicare Part A and Part B spending for attributed beneficiaries, regardless of where care is delivered. Out-of-network spending counts against the ACO.
correct_fact: MSSP benchmarks and performance expenditures are Medicare Parts A and B FFS expenditures of assigned beneficiaries.
source_quote: reduce the rate of growth in expenditures under Medicare Parts A and B. For each performance year of the agreement period, ACOs share in a percentage of the savings they generate if the expenditures of the ACO's assigned beneficiaries are below their benchmark
notes: Saved as sources/cms_mssp_shared_savings_methodology_v9_2021.txt.

quote: AHEAD would have tracked total cost of care for Medicare FFS beneficiaries attributed to Vermont hospitals across all payer settings; Act 68's global budgets apply the same all-payer accounting.
correct_fact: AHEAD's accountability targets were statewide: a Medicare FFS total cost of care target (2023 baseline, $12,040 PBPY) and an all-payer TCOC growth target -- not TCOC for beneficiaries attributed to hospitals. Act 68 global budgets are hospital revenue budgets that 'shall not include Medicaid', so they are not all-payer.
source_quote: GMCB AHEAD board deck 12/6/2024: 'Statewide Accountability Targets: Total Cost of Care Growth (Medicare & All-Payer)'; 'Medicare FFS Total Cost of Care target ... VT will use a 2023 baseline year weighted at 100% ... 2023 PBPY: $12,040'. Act 68: 'Global hospital budgets ... shall include Medicare to the extent permitted under federal law but shall not include Medicaid.'
proposed_new_text: AHEAD would have held Vermont to statewide Medicare FFS and all-payer total cost of care targets; Act 68's global budgets are hospital revenue budgets that include Medicare where federal law permits but exclude Medicaid.
notes: Contradicts VERIFIED_FACTS (global budgets exclude Medicaid).

quote: In most shared savings models, savings must exceed a minimum threshold (typically 2-3.5%) before the organization shares in them
correct_fact: In MSSP's one-sided BASIC levels the MSR is a sliding scale from 3.9% (5,000 assigned beneficiaries) to 2.0% (60,000+); two-sided ACOs elect a symmetric MSR/MLR of 0-2%. ACO REACH has no MSR.
source_quote: Example: Determining MSR for ACOs in a One-Sided Model ... MSR Low End (5,000): 3.9% ... Table 6. MSR by number of assigned beneficiaries as specified in § 425.605(b)(1) ... 60,000 + 2.0% 2.0%
proposed_new_text: In most shared savings models, savings must exceed a minimum threshold before the organization shares in them (in MSSP's one-sided track, 2.0-3.9% depending on ACO size)
notes: The platform's own APM Shared Savings Calculator already uses 2.0-3.9% (APMCalculator.tsx line 33), so the book contradicts its tool.

quote: AHEAD used a different structure --- state-level TCOC targets rather than individual ACO MSRs --- and Act 68's state-level global budget targets apply the minimum threshold concept the same way.
correct_fact: The AHEAD half is correct (statewide TCOC targets). Act 68 contains no 'state-level global budget targets' with a minimum-savings threshold; it requires GMCB to set individual hospital global budgets and the Statewide Health Care Delivery Strategic Plan (due Jan 15, 2028) to set annual TCOC targets.
source_quote: the Board shall establish global hospital budgets for one or more Vermont hospitals that are not critical access hospitals. By hospital fiscal year 2030, to the extent that resources are available, the Board shall establish global hospital budgets for all Vermont hospitals.
proposed_new_text: AHEAD used a different structure --- state-level TCOC targets rather than individual ACO MSRs. Act 68 has no MSR equivalent: it sets hospital-by-hospital global budgets, with statewide TCOC targets to come from the Statewide Health Care Delivery Strategic Plan.
notes: TCOC targets in strategic plan per VERIFIED_FACTS (9403(b)(7)).

quote: Sharing rates vary by model and risk track --- typically 50-75% for one-sided models, and reaches 100% in global-risk models such as ACO REACH.
correct_fact: MSSP's one-sided BASIC Levels A-B pay up to 40% of savings; two-sided BASIC Levels C-E pay 50%; the ENHANCED track pays 75% (two-sided). 75% is a two-sided rate, not one-sided. ACO REACH Global = 100% savings/losses (CONFIRMED), but ACO REACH ends after PY2026 and is succeeded by CMS's LEAD model (2027-2036), which keeps a 100% Global Risk option.
source_quote: 42 CFR 425.605: 'BASIC track, Level A, receives a shared savings payment of up to 40 percent of all the savings'; 'BASIC track, Level C, receives a shared savings payment of up to 50 percent'; MSSP spec: 'Maximum sharing rate: 75%' (ENHANCED). ACO REACH: 'A higher risk sharing arrangement — 100% savings/losses'; '(PY 2023 through PY 2026)'. LEAD: 'set to launch following the conclusion of ACO REACH at the end of 2026.'
proposed_new_text: Sharing rates vary by model and risk track --- up to 40% in MSSP's one-sided levels, 50-75% in its two-sided tracks, and 100% in global-risk models such as ACO REACH's Global option (succeeded in 2027 by CMS's LEAD model).
notes: Same error repeats at line 3742 (Key Concepts). Tool APMCalculator.tsx already corrected to 40% on 2026-10-08. The Five Pillars Academy lesson apm-readiness-vbc-financial-modeling carries the same old figures (Sanity body: 'up to 50% of savings' one-sided; MSR 'roughly 2% to 3.5%') -- flag for Academy owner; not edited (read-only).

quote: Vermont RBP: savings to payers from price reduction; 100% of premium passthrough per GMCB monitoring requirement.
correct_fact: Act 68 does not require 100% premium passthrough. It requires GMCB, with DFR, to monitor that hospital price decreases also result in premium decreases and to post findings annually.
source_quote: The Board, in collaboration with the Department of Financial Regulation, shall monitor the implementation of reference-based pricing to ensure that any decreases in amounts paid to hospitals also result in decreases in health insurance premiums. The Board shall post its findings regarding the alignment between price decreases and premium decreases annually on its website.
proposed_new_text: Vermont RBP: savings to payers from price reduction; GMCB and DFR must monitor whether those price decreases reach premiums and report annually.
notes: Related claim at line 3732 ('Act 68's passthrough requirement').

quote: the financial return on a care management program that costs \$200,000 to operate is approximately 3.75:1 --- a 275% ROI.
notes: Arithmetic only; the $15,000 input is illustrative and unsourced (see next finding).

Only the 32.3% potentially avoidable ED visits figure is confirmed (AHS Nov 2025 Act 68 report, per VERIFIED_FACTS).

correct_fact: No RHRC HCC-gap assessment found. AHS's RHRC contract (announced Feb 17, 2025) covered technical assistance, financial planning and change management; it concluded Oct 9, 2025. Neither the RHRC announcement nor the AHS Nov 2025 Act 68 report mentions HCC coding or a 12% gap.

correct_fact: RBP effective HFY2028 is CONFIRMED (GMCB: methodology set by rule in 2027, effective HFY28). The RBP savings estimate is GMCB/HMA's: ~$400M over 2018-Q3 2023 for VSEA+VEHI plans at 200% of Medicare ($79M in 2022).

GMCB RBP report 12/16/2024: 'Adjusting these payments to 200% of Medicare could have saved the VSEA/VEHI health plans approximately $400 million during the study period, with $79 million of savings estimated in 2022.'

correct_fact: Arithmetic: a 30% withhold on a 50% share puts 15% of gross savings -- i.e. 30% of the organization's own shared-savings payment -- at stake on quality. 'Total financial outcome' is ambiguous and understates the exposure from the organization's point of view.
proposed_new_text: A 30% quality withhold on a 50% share of gross savings puts 15% of gross savings --- 30% of the organization's own payment --- at stake on quality performance; understand the measures before signing.
notes: Logic/arithmetic clarity fix; same sentence is reused in the Academy lesson.

quote: As Act 68's mandatory global budgets take effect for non-CAH hospitals beginning FY2028, hospital CFOs need to transition from FFS revenue optimization to global budget management.

The Introduction (line 675) states it correctly: 'as resources allow, global budgets for every hospital'.
source_quote: Beginning not later than hospital fiscal year 2028, to the extent that resources are available, the Board shall establish global hospital budgets for one or more Vermont hospitals that are not critical access hospitals. Not later than hospital fiscal year 2030, to the extent that resources are available, the Board shall establish global hospital budgets for all Vermont hospitals.
proposed_new_text: As Act 68's global budgets arrive --- for one or more non-CAH hospitals beginning not later than FY2028 and for every hospital by FY2030, in each case to the extent resources are available --- hospital CFOs need to transition from FFS revenue optimization to global budget management.
notes: Similar framing at line 3728 ('the global budget environment your organization will be operating under from FY2028') -- true only for the first non-CAH hospital(s); CAHs come by FY2030.

correct_fact: OW: 'ideally at 200% of Medicare or less for PPS hospitals'. GMCB's Dec 16, 2024 RBP report (HMA analysis) modeled 150%, 180%, 200% and 250% of Medicare; 250% is the highest scenario ($234M savings total vs $400M at 200%). The Stress Test offers both 200% and 250% benchmark buttons.

'One of the recommendations was to begin movement to reference-based pricing ideally at 200% of Medicare or less for PPS hospitals.'

quote: With H.R. 1's Medicaid revenue reductions phasing in from 2027--2031, what is our projected total revenue under conservative, base, and optimistic assumptions about our Medicaid payer mix?
correct_fact: H.R. 1's eligibility provisions (work requirements) start Jan 1, 2027, but the provider-tax safe-harbor phase-down for expansion states such as Vermont runs FFY2028 (5.5%) to FFY2032 (3.5%), and state-directed-payment reductions begin with rating periods on/after Jan 1, 2028. The phase-in window is 2027-2032, not 2027-2031.
source_quote: Under H.R. 1, in states that have adopted the Medicaid expansion, the current safe harbor threshold of 6 percent will be reduced to 5.5 percent in fiscal year 2028, 5 percent in 2029, 4.5 percent in 2030, 4 percent in 2031 and then to 3.5 percent in fiscal year 2032 and thereafter.
proposed_new_text: With H.R. 1's Medicaid revenue reductions phasing in from 2027--2032, what is our projected total revenue under conservative, base, and optimistic assumptions about our Medicaid payer mix?
notes: Stress Test tool hard-codes HR1_YEARS 2027-2031 (HospitalFinancialScorecard.tsx:141); tool should add 2032. Work requirements Jan 1, 2027 per VERIFIED_FACTS. Saved CCF text to sources/ccf_hr1_provider_tax_guidance_2025-11-18.txt.

correct_fact: 32.3% potentially avoidable ED visits is the AHS Nov 2025 Act 68 report figure (Oliver Wyman analysis of 2020-2022 VUHDDS/VHCURES). Arithmetic correct: 500 x $1,800 = $900K; ($900K - $300K)/$300K = 200%.

correct_fact: Jones et al., Popul Health Manag 2016;19(3):196-205 (2008-2013 data): ~$5.8M lower medical expenditures per $1M spent, an annualized cost-gain ratio. Arithmetic 3 x 5.8 = 17.4 correct. correct_fact: Arithmetic is right (200 x 30% = 60 readmissions; 10% = 6; 6 x $15,000 = $90,000), but a $10,000/year RPM program for 200 patients ($50 per patient per year) is not a credible cost: Medicare RPM device-supply and management codes alone run on the order of $100+ per patient per month. Vermont's RHT plan includes RPM ($0.9M in year 1), so the 'RHT Program RPM grants' label is supported.
source_quote: VERIFIED_FACTS: 'RHT application activity list: ... RPM ($0.9M yr1)'
proposed_new_text: Vermont RHT Program RPM grants: CHF readmission prevention via RPM in a population of 200 high-risk patients, preventing 10% of 30-day readmissions at 30% readmission rate, saves \$90,000/year --- ROI positive only if the RPM program costs less than that.
notes: RPM per-patient cost cited from general knowledge of CMS RPM codes (99453/99454/99457), not read in a primary source this session -- hence INCONSISTENT (internal plausibility), not WRONG.

quote: The AHEAD Model's requirement that states demonstrate increased investment in primary care as a percentage of total spending is not just a quality metric --- it is an economics imperative.
correct_fact: AHEAD's statewide accountability targets included Primary Care Investment (Medicare & All-Payer). Vermont withdrew from AHEAD in July 2026, which the chapter acknowledges at line 3700.

notes: Same paragraph's superlative 'primary care is the highest-return investment a healthcare system can make' is unsourced (UNCONFIRMED); consider 'among the highest-return'.
